newsitem.title: USA: Governors want Conrail merger protections. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Governors want Conrail merger protections. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]

text.p: A group of northeastern governors issued a joint statement Tuesday saying any acquisition of Conrail should protect competition and passenger service and preserve growth opportunities.
Conrail said last week in a statement it was continuing to seek approval of a merger with CSX Corp. Norfolk Southern Corp is a rival to acquire Conrail (corrects from CSX.)

The governors took no position on which company should acquire Conrail (corrects from CSX.) Instead, they asserted that "competition, choice and capacity in the resulting rail system is essential if the northeast is to have affordable, effective service which advances the long-term competitiveness of the region within the national and global economy."

They said that two or more strong carriers should be assured between major service areas; passenger services should be protected; short and regional lines should have competitive connections to national markets and the system must be able to grow.

The statement was authorized by the Coaliton of Northeastern Governors, which includes Connecticut Gov. John Rowland, Maine Gov. Angus King, Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen, New Jersey Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, New York Gov. George Pataki, Pennsylvania Gov. Thomas Ridge, Rhode Island Gov. Lincoln Almond and Vermont Gov. Howard Dean.
